title: Hadacol show and Dudley LeBlanc
summary: Riddick describes the Hadacol caravan, its 12 percent alcohol content, and generous, funny Dudley LeBlanc.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: That's Montgomery... Tiny Boswell. Montgomery Advertiser. Yeah. The Hattacall.

The Hattacall show was well received. That's in Montgomery, Alabama. See, we played in nothing but stadiums, football stadiums. We had as many... The price of admission was to buy a bottle of Hattacall. And you took the top of the box, the carton, and tore it off, and it had on the Hattacall. And that was your... What would it cost to get in? I think it was $2 a bottle. Well, we had as many as 40,000 people there. You know what I had a call from? All right. You know, that's Geritol today.
I've heard of it, but wasn't it mostly liquor? Alcohol?

Wasn't it real high in alcohol? No. It was a vitamin supplement. But it was... 12% alcohol as a preservative. Mm-hmm. About like one. But on LeBlanc... Dudley LeBlanc had three trucks that he went with the caravan. Mm-hmm. And two of the trucks were full of whiskey. Mm-hmm. And the third truck was full of Hattacall for those that drank the whiskey. Because if you take a shot of Hattacall or half of a glass of Hattacall before you started to drink, and after you got through drinking, you got up in the morning and you took a glass of Hattacall. And in 30 minutes' time, you were back on your feet going on about your business. They could still sell it now then, if that was a...

Well, you could use it in martinis instead of vermouth. I'm not kidding you. During the rage, I know people who did that. It got to be kind of a joke, too. Uh-huh. Dudley LeBlanc had a good sense of humor.
Very much so. He might have been a caginant. He was so full of fun. And he was a nice guy. Yeah. He'd give you anything in the world.
Well, what happened to his partner?
